title: Fixing burst starts gives an exact test of continuation under an initiation-weighted interval null
abstract: We derived a continuation test from a published joint burst-count law. With fixed short and other interval counts S and O and e observed burst starts, the number of anchored short intervals minus e has a beta-binomial law with S-e trials and shape parameters e and O+1. The long count cancels. The conditional upper-tail test has finite size at most alpha under every weighting of uniform interval orders that depends only on the number of starts. We prove a vector version for separate records. All 265,720 category words through length 11 matched the law, and 71,071 finite-count cases passed a 5 percent size check. In a chosen finite benchmark that changed recruitment alone, the global burst test rejected with probability 0.930, while the conditional test rejected with probability 0.022. A global rejection is valid for its stronger null; it does not by itself show excess continuation. Conditioning can improve sensitivity to selected continuation changes, but can also lose power. The result requires uniform conditional arrangements within event-count strata. It does not control arbitrary state changes. No raw mouse data were used, and no channel or wiring mechanism is established. Code, proof, finite benchmark results, provenance and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Finite count tests separate initiation changes from continuation under the stated null. All plotted probabilities are finite sums, not mouse estimates.
